sentences.text: The genus name Teratosaurus comes from Greek words meaning 'monster' and 'lizard'.
The holotype fossil — the specimen the species is based on — suggests the animal reached a body length of about six meters.
The holotype of Teratosaurus was discovered in 1860 by Sixt Friedrich Jakob von Kapff near Stuttgart, Germany.
Research in 1985 and 1986 proved Teratosaurus was a rauisuchian, a four-legged predatory archosaur that lived alongside dinosaurs.
Teratosaurus belongs to the order Rauisuchia.
It is classified within the family Rauisuchidae.
The species Teratosaurus silesiacus was moved to the genus Polonosuchus in 2009.
Teratosaurus lived between 251.902 and 205.7 million years ago, from the Induan to the Norian stages.
Early researchers incorrectly assigned fossils of the sauropodomorph dinosaur Efraasia to Teratosaurus.
For much of the 20th century, Teratosaurus was mistakenly believed to be a large, bipedal meat-eating dinosaur.
Many scientists once thought Teratosaurus was an ancestor of the Jurassic carnosaurs.
